{\huge\color{accent}A Reader’s Guide to Thought, Freedom \& Craft}\par\vspace{4mm}
{\small “Friends often ask which books shaped me. These are the ones I keep going back to. Read with a pencil, keep what serves you, leave the rest.”}\par\vspace{2mm}
{\footnotesize\color{inkmuted}Marc Duboc (@promaa), Seoul}\par\vspace{5mm}

\begin{longtable}{@{}L@{\hspace{6mm}}L@{}}
\multicolumn{2}{@{}p{\textwidth}@{}}{\trackheader{Foundational Pillars \& Liberty}}\\*[2mm]
\bookentry{01-frankl.jpg}{Man’s Search for Meaning}{Viktor E. Frankl (1946)}{Memoir · Resilience}{{\small\color{inkmuted}Best for: When feeling overwhelmed or losing your sense of purpose.}\par\vspace{1mm}}{Frankl survived Auschwitz and distilled the most liberating psychological truth ever written: you cannot always control your circumstances, but you always have absolute sovereignty over your attitude. Read when feeling adrift; trivial anxieties evaporate.}{Finding a “why” that outlasts any collapse of the “how.”} & \bookentry{02-dumas.jpg}{The Count of Monte Cristo}{Alexandre Dumas (1844)}{Classic Novel · Strategy}{}{The greatest adventure in literature, but really a masterclass in composure, patience, and playing the 20-year game. Edmond Dantès never panics; he calculates, accumulates leverage, and masters time.}{“All human wisdom is contained in these two words: Wait and hope.”}\\[3mm]
\bookentry{03-friedman.jpg}{Capitalism and Freedom}{Milton Friedman (1962)}{Essay · Economics \& Liberty}{}{Friedman cuts through bureaucratic rhetoric with razor clarity. Even without agreeing with every market conclusion, it forces you to question why we surrender so much daily autonomy to administrative inertia.}{Economic freedom and personal autonomy are fundamentally inseparable.} & \bookentry{04-laboetie.jpg}{Discourse on Voluntary Servitude}{Étienne de La Boétie (1576)}{Political Philosophy}{}{Written by an 18-year-old in the 16th century, and still fresher than almost any modern commentary. His core insight is devastating: tyrants only hold power because the governed consent to obey them.}{A short, electrifying shock to the system against passive compliance.}\\[3mm]
\bookentry{05-constant.jpg}{On the Liberty of the Ancients compared with that of the Moderns}{Benjamin Constant (1819)}{Speech / Essay · Political Theory}{}{Constant drew a brilliant distinction: ancient freedom was constant political mobilization; modern freedom is the sacred right to be left in peace to pursue your craft, family, and ideas without interference.}{The foundational case for private sanctuary over permanent political noise.} & \\[3mm]
\multicolumn{2}{@{}p{\textwidth}@{}}{\trackheader{Systems, Power \& Technology}}\\*[2mm]
\bookentry{06-chomsky.jpg}{Manufacturing Consent}{Noam Chomsky \& Edward S. Herman (1988)}{Media Theory · Systems}{}{Breaks down the 5 structural filters through which mass media selects, frames, and purifies information. A diagnostic toolkit so you never consume news passively again.}{Your personal mental firewall against manufactured consensus.} & \bookentry{07-snowden.jpg}{Permanent Record}{Edward Snowden (2019)}{Memoir · Cybersecurity}{}{Beyond NSA disclosures, this is about treating technology with ethical seriousness. Convenience is a trap: if you don’t maintain your tools, your tools will control you.}{Treat your machines and privacy with the rigor of a craftsman.}\\[3mm]
\bookentry{08-rand.jpg}{Atlas Shrugged}{Ayn Rand (1957)}{Philosophical Fiction · Individualism}{}{A monumental philosophical novel defending the primacy of reason, productive individual agency, and the creator’s mind against bureaucratic collectivism and coerced guilt.}{The mind is the prime mover of human progress; never sacrifice your agency to unearned guilt.} & \bookentry{09-branco.jpg}{Crépuscule}{Juan Branco (2019)}{Investigative Pamphlet}{{\small\color{inkmuted}Best for: Inspecting the revolving doors and inner circles of French power.}\par\vspace{1mm}}{Whatever one thinks of Branco’s polemical tone, the structural breakdown of Parisian oligarchic networks and revolving doors is documented with surgical precision.}{A candid look inside the closed circles and machinery of French power.}\\[3mm]
\bookentry{10-huntington.jpg}{The Clash of Civilizations}{Samuel P. Huntington (1996)}{Geopolitics · Macro-History}{}{Predicted that post-Cold War conflicts would run along civilizational and cultural fault lines. An indispensable macro-lens to decode modern international flashpoints.}{A pragmatic compass for navigating global geopolitical fractures.} & \bookentry{11-gave.jpg}{A Liberal Named Jesus}{Charles Gave (2019)}{Essay · Economics \& Agency}{}{An unorthodox, punchy read re-examining the Gospels through the lens of individual agency, capital allocation, and productive risk as moral duties.}{A refreshing perspective on risk-taking, stewardship, and accountability.}\\[3mm]
\multicolumn{2}{@{}p{\textwidth}@{}}{\trackheader{Solitude, Discipline \& Craft}}\\*[2mm]
\bookentry{12-powys.jpg}{A Philosophy of Solitude}{John Cowper Powys (1933)}{Philosophy · Stillness}{{\small\color{inkmuted}Best for: Sinking into sensory calm during hyper-connected burnout.}\par\vspace{1mm}}{Practical rituals for cultivating an unshakeable inner fortress: elemental pauses, walking alone, observing wind and stone. Solitude here is the deliberate cultivation of one's own mind.}{The antidote to hyper-connected overstimulation and mental burnout.} & \bookentry{13-gombrich.jpg}{The Story of Art}{E. H. Gombrich (1950)}{Art History · Visual Culture}{}{The antithesis of pretentious art theory. Gombrich writes like an attentive, wise friend strolling through an empty gallery, explaining how humanity learned to see light and perspective.}{The single best companion book before visiting any museum in the world.}\\[3mm]
\bookentry{14-sarthou-lajus.jpg}{Vertigo of Dependence}{Nathalie Sarthou-Lajus (2012)}{Essay · Relationships}{}{A lucid reflection on the illusions of absolute self-sufficiency. Acknowledging our vulnerabilities and chosen bonds is the true starting point of emotional maturity.}{A quiet mirror reminding us that true strength lies in accepting limits.} & \\[3mm]
\multicolumn{2}{@{}p{\textwidth}@{}}{\trackheader{Great Narratives \& The Human Condition}}\\*[2mm]
\bookentry{15-crime-punishment.jpg}{Crime and Punishment}{Fyodor Dostoevsky (1866)}{Psychological Novel}{}{Inside Raskolnikov’s feverish brain as intellectual arrogance disintegrates against the crushing weight of human conscience. Unbearably tense and utterly profound.}{The greatest warning against elevating abstract ideology over human reality.} & \bookentry{16-karamazov.jpg}{The Brothers Karamazov}{Fyodor Dostoevsky (1880)}{Classic Novel · Philosophy}{}{Dmitri (passion), Ivan (intellect), Alyosha (faith). Every fundamental conflict of human nature is played out in this family. The 'Grand Inquisitor' chapter alone is legendary.}{The absolute pinnacle of psychological and philosophical literature.}\\[3mm]
\bookentry{17-gambler.jpg}{The Gambler}{Fyodor Dostoevsky (1867)}{Novella · Addiction}{}{Written in just 26 days to pay off roulette debts, this short novel is a frantic dissection of how obsession and the illusion of control trap even sharp minds.}{Fast, sharp, and brutally observant of the psychology of compulsive hope.} & \bookentry{18-gary-promesse.jpg}{Promise at Dawn}{Romain Gary (1960)}{Autobiographical Novel}{{\small\color{inkmuted}Best for: Rekindling fierce filial love, courage, and literary panache.}\par\vspace{1mm}}{Gary’s tribute to his mother’s boundless, irrational faith in him. It oscillates between laugh-out-loud humor and overwhelming emotional power.}{The kind of book that makes you put it down and call your mother immediately.}\\[3mm]
\bookentry{19-gary-vie.jpg}{The Life Before Us}{Romain Gary (Émile Ajar) (1975)}{Novel · Tenderness}{}{Narrated by young Momo veiling over Madame Rosa in Belleville. It has more genuine warmth, human solidarity, and streetwise wisdom in 200 pages than entire literary eras.}{A masterclass in humor, tenderness, and finding beauty in the margins.} & \bookentry{20-verne.jpg}{Around the World in Eighty Days}{Jules Verne (1872)}{Adventure · Stoicism}{}{Read before hiking the GR20. Phileas Fogg’s mathematical composure and Passepartout’s loyalty make it the ultimate comfort read on resourcefulness and perseverance.}{Pure Victorian rhythm, calm under pressure, and the joy of problem-solving.}\\[3mm]
\bookentry{21-faye.jpg}{Small Country}{Gaël Faye (2016)}{Contemporary Novel}{}{A luminous, heartbreaking story of childhood in Burundi shattered by war. Faye demonstrates how literature, music, and nature serve as the last shields of human dignity.}{A poetic testament to memory and resilience in times of upheaval.} & \\[3mm]
\end{longtable}
